text: Write a ring buffer's index arithmetic, which is where its invariant lives. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: private final String[] items = new String[3];
int tail = ___;                     // where the next item goes, wrapping
if (size < items.length) size++; else head = ___;   // full: overwrite oldest
String get(int i) { return items[(head + i) % items.length]; }
explanation: Verified: it prints `bcd` — the oldest entry was overwritten. Every field here is meaningless alone; the structure lives entirely in the promise that the logical contents are `items[head]` through `items[(head+size-1) % length]`. That is why writing the invariant down first is the practical technique: the index arithmetic is impossible to get right by intuition and straightforward once the promise is stated.
